title: The transsulfuration pathway metabolite alpha-ketobutyrate drives RIPK1-lactate axis-dependent autophagy to alleviate Staphylococcus aureus infection.
authors: Fu, Shaodong; Yang, Chengsen; Zhao, Shiyang; Fang, Yingzou; Li, Ming; Lu, Jinye; Yang, Bo; Qiu, Yawei; Wang, Huanhuan; Zhang, Jinqiu; Xu, Yuanyuan; Miao, Jinfeng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究代谢物alpha-KB通过RIPK1-乳酸-TFEB轴调控自噬缓解金黄色葡萄球菌感染，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是代谢-免疫通路而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Breastfeeding anchors infant immunity and long-term health, but its benefits are threatened by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) mastitis, an increasingly prevalent condition driven by antimicrobial resistance and therapeutic limitations. Beyond compromising maternal wellness, mastitis threatens the safety and continuity of breast milk, highlighting a critical need for innovative intervention strategies. Herein, we demonstrated that alpha‑ketobutyrate (alpha-KB), a metabolite of the transsulfuration pathway, mitigated S. aureus‑induced inflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-milk barrier (BMB) disruption both in vivo and in vitro. alpha‑KB enhanced macroautophagic/autophagic responses, marked by increased ATG5, BECN1 (beclin 1), and LC3-II:LC3-I conversion and reduced SQSTM1/p62, through a RIPK1-lactate-TFEB axis. Specifically, it directly bound and stabilized RIPK1, elevated lactate production, and drove TFEB nuclear translocation to activate macroautophagy/autophagy and promote intracellular bacterial clearance. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable alpha‑KB and RIPK1 binding via hydrophobic and hydrogen bond interactions; RIPK1 knockout abolished alpha‑KB-induced autophagy and lactate generation, effects rescued by lactate supplementation. This study identifies a novel immunometabolic circuit linking a metabolite to RIPK1-lactate-TFEB-mediated autophagy, offering therapeutic potential against antibiotic‑resistant S. aureus mastitis and presenting a new paradigm for safeguarding breastfeeding quality and infant health.Abbreviations: 3-MA: 3-methyladenine; alpha-KB: alpha‑ketobutyrate; ATG5: autophagy related 5; BMB: blood-milk barrier; CETSA: cellular thermal shift assay; DARTS: drug affinity responsive target stability; IL1B: interleukin 1 beta; IL6: interleukin 6; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3; MST: microscale thermophoresis; NOS2: nitric oxide synthase 2; OCLN: occludin; PBS: phosphate-buffered saline; PTGS2: prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2; Rapa: rapamycin; RIPK1: receptor interacting serine/threonine kinase 1; RT-PCR: real-time polymerasechain reaction;S. aureus:Staphylococcus aureus; SEM: standard error of the mean; SQSTM1/p62: sequestosome 1; TFEB: transcription factor EB; TJP1: tight junction protein 1; TNF: tumor necrosis factor; WT: wild-type.
abstract_zh: 母乳喂养是婴儿免疫和长期健康的基础，但其益处受到金黄色葡萄球菌（Staphylococcus aureus, S. aureus）乳腺炎的威胁，这是一种因抗菌药物耐药性和治疗局限性而日益普遍的疾病。除了损害母亲健康外，乳腺炎还危及母乳的安全性和连续性，凸显了对创新干预策略的迫切需求。在此，我们证明α-酮丁酸（alpha-ketobutyrate, alpha-KB），一种转硫途径的代谢物，在体内和体外均减轻了S. aureus诱导的炎症、氧化应激和血乳屏障（blood-milk barrier, BMB）破坏。alpha-KB通过RIPK1-乳酸-TFEB轴增强了巨自噬/自噬反应，表现为ATG5、BECN1（beclin 1）和LC3-II:LC3-I转化增加，以及SQSTM1/p62减少。具体而言，它直接结合并稳定RIPK1，提高乳酸产生，并驱动TFEB核转位以激活巨自噬/自噬并促进细胞内细菌清除。分子对接和分子动力学模拟表明，alpha-KB与RIPK1通过疏水相互作用和氢键相互作用稳定结合；RIPK1敲除消除了alpha-KB诱导的自噬和乳酸生成，而乳酸补充可挽救这些效应。本研究识别了一种新的免疫代谢回路，将代谢物与RIPK1-乳酸-TFEB介导的自噬联系起来，为抗抗生素耐药性S. aureus乳腺炎提供了治疗潜力，并为保障母乳喂养质量和婴儿健康提出了新范式。缩写：3-MA: 3-甲基腺嘌呤；alpha-KB: α-酮丁酸；ATG5: 自噬相关5；BMB: 血乳屏障；CETSA: 细胞热位移分析；DARTS: 药物亲和响应靶标稳定性；IL1B: 白细胞介素1β；IL6: 白细胞介素6；MAP1LC3/LC3: 微管相关蛋白1轻链3；MST: 微量热泳动；NOS2: 一氧化氮合酶2；OCLN: 闭合蛋白；PBS: 磷酸盐缓冲液；PTGS2: 前列腺素内过氧化物合酶2；Rapa: 雷帕霉素；RIPK1: 受体相互作用丝氨酸/苏氨酸激酶1；RT-PCR: 实时聚合酶链反应；S. aureus: 金黄色葡萄球菌；SEM: 平均标准误；SQSTM1/p62: 死骨片1；TFEB: 转录因子EB；TJP1: 紧密连接蛋白1；TNF: 肿瘤坏死因子；WT: 野生型。
